usage: Code health guardrails for personal-website-spike, applied by cs review, cs check and the CodeScene PR gates. Every rule set here is a guardrail against coding-agent entropy: this repository is a Next.js 16.3.4 App Router scaffold that was produced entirely by coding agents, so the failure modes these rules catch are agent failure modes. The README records that the original /lab piece was a Codex artefact that had to be rebuilt in this workspace, the three diagrams under public/diagrams/ are Archify 3.0.1 output, and Next 16 generated its own AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md into the tree - both deleted in daff7a5, where next.config.ts gained agentRules: false - so the scaffold, the diagrams and the instruction files all arrived from tools rather than from hand edits. The shapes that hurt here are the ones an agent produces next: a route page that absorbs its own data shaping and interaction state, a canvas component that accretes one more draw pass into an animation-frame closure that is already 112 code lines, a second copy of the pipeline stage list instead of an import from lib/notebook-pipeline.ts. Every rule set keys off a file path and a code-level metric only. Evaluation is first-match-wins from top to bottom, so the list is ordered narrowest-glob-first: the generated Archify diagram output, then the client component family, then the App Router page family, and the broad **/* catch-all last so that any new directory - a tests/ tree, a .github/ workflow, a second lib module with real logic - starts under the full 23-rule guardrail. Rule weights are 1.0 everywhere except the single generated path, which is excluded at 0.0; no structural smell is muted in application code, and none will be muted in test code either, because there is no test rule set to inherit a relaxation from.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: Generated, not written here. The three files this set covers are public/diagrams/distribution.html, public/diagrams/repair-batch.html and public/diagrams/ship-boundary.html. Each one carries <meta name="generator" content="archify 3.0.1"> on line 6 of its head, each SVG description reads "A workflow diagram generated by Archify." (ship-boundary.html line 4992), and diagrams/README.md states the contract outright: the editable inputs are the JSON beside them and "editing generated HTML by hand will be lost on regeneration". They are 13,678 to 13,723 lines and 753 KB to 758 KB each - 41,112 of the 41,853 lines across every tracked .ts/.tsx/.mjs/.css/.html file in the repository - so a size rule pointed at them measures Archify, not this site. All 23 rules are weighted 0.0 so that a diagram export is never a refactoring target and a size finding can never be cleared by hand-editing markup that the next Archify finalize run overwrites. cs 1.0.55 has no HTML analyzer (cs review answers "Unsupported file-type \".html\"" for all three), so today this set is a declared boundary rather than an active scoring path; it is written now so the boundary is already in force if an HTML analyzer arrives, and `cs check-rules public/diagrams/ship-boundary.html` already resolves to it. To revise a diagram, re-run Archify finalize with diagrams/<name>.json as the input.

rule_sets.rules_doc: All 23 rules at 0.0 is the only defensible weighting for a generated export: a 13,700-line self-contained HTML document will trip Lines of Code in a Single File, Large Embedded Code Block and Overall Code Complexity on every reasonable threshold, and none of those findings would name a change to this repository. A coding agent that "fixed" one by splitting the file would break the self-contained contract that lets the page be served from public/ with no Archify at runtime, and the next finalize run would restore the original bytes.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The four client components: components/lab/context-engine-canvas.tsx (233 physical lines, 164 code lines, the only substantial logic in the repository), components/lab/context-engine-lab.tsx (89 lines), components/providers/motion-root.tsx (8) and components/stub-page.tsx (22). Three of them open with a "use client" directive and own browser state - a canvas 2D render loop with requestAnimationFrame, a matchMedia reduced-motion branch, an interval-driven stage cycler, a MotionConfig provider - so this is where an agent's next draw pass, effect or piece of interaction state lands. All 23 rules stay at 1.0; the calibration in this set is the thresholds, which are measured from the two purpose-built lab components instead of left at framework defaults that never fire on a 164-code-line file cs already scores 10.0.

rule_sets.rules_doc: Nothing is muted, because this directory is the opposite of a false-positive farm: it is the one place in the repository with loops, conditionals and accumulating state. Large Method at 1.0 is doing the work that matters most here - it is the rule that reports the 112-code-line animation-frame closure - and Bumpy Road Ahead, Deep Nested Complexity and Complex Method stay at 1.0 so that the next nested reduced-motion branch, or the next per-node special case inside the draw loop, is a health finding rather than a diff nobody measures. Deep, Global Nested Complexity and Global Conditionals stay at 1.0 because module-level conditionals in a client component are how browser capability checks become untestable. Code Duplication stays at 1.0 because the pipeline stage list already has one home (lib/notebook-pipeline.ts) and a local copy in a component is exactly the drift this rule catches.
rule_sets.thresholds_doc: file_lines_of_code_for_warning 200: the canvas measures 164 code lines - cs reports "This module has 164 lines of code (comments stripped away)" - and still scores 10.0 with no .codescene/ present, so the framework default is at least 165 for this analyzer; 200 is the observed maximum plus the headroom of roughly one more draw pass, and it keeps a component from growing into a 600-line scene file before anyone is warned. function_lines_of_code_warning 90: the measured component functions are ContextEngineCanvas.tick at 112 code lines (canvas L80-202) and ContextEngineLab at 75 (lab L9-89). 90 falls between them on purpose - a component under 90 lines is still a view, while the 112-line closure that draws grid, edges, particles, node labels and HUD in one body is the shape an agent grows instead of splitting, so it is reported (canvas 10.0 -> 9.38, Large Method) rather than allowed to pass until the default fires somewhere above 112. function_max_arguments 3: a React component has one contract, its props object; a function here that needs a fourth positional argument has lost that contract. None of the four current components trips it.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The App Router tree - eleven tracked files: app/layout.tsx (33 lines) and the route segments app/page.tsx (63), app/lab/page.tsx (53), app/lab/agent-delivery/page.tsx (73), app/lab/context-engine/page.tsx (11), app/work, app/radar, app/library and app/digest (5 each), plus app/globals.css, which cs cannot score (it answers "Unsupported file-type \".css\""). Every page is a server component that imports its data and its one client island: the four stub routes render components/stub-page.tsx, /lab/context-engine renders ContextEngineLab, and the two largest pages are a NAV table and a three-diagram list. That is the shape Next expects, which is exactly why the cap here is tighter than the component cap: a route segment that starts fetching, shaping and interactively mutating in its own body is the drift this set blocks, and the answer is a client component or a lib/ module, not a 300-line page.

rule_sets.rules_doc: All 23 at 1.0, no exceptions. The rules that matter for a page are the size and structure ones - a page that grows a second data table, a third metadata export or an inline client hook chain should show up as Large Method, Bumpy Road Ahead or Complex Method instead of being normalised across nine route files. Low Cohesion, Primitive Obsession and String Heavy Function Arguments are left at 1.0 as well: React components take one props object, so those rules do not misfire here, and leaving them on means the moment a page takes four positional strings the signature rule says so.
rule_sets.thresholds_doc: file_lines_of_code_for_warning 90: the largest page is app/page.tsx at 52 code lines (cs reports "This module has 52 lines of code (comments stripped away)") and app/lab/agent-delivery/page.tsx at 41, so 90 leaves both at 10.0 with room for one more section while stopping the drift toward a page-as-application; the four 5-line stub routes are nowhere near it. function_lines_of_code_warning 60: the largest route function is Home at 52 code lines (app/page.tsx L11-63) with AgentDeliveryPage at 41 (L33-73), so 60 is under two screens of markup away - a page function past 60 lines has almost certainly absorbed a layout that should have been exported as a component. function_max_arguments 3: a page takes its params object and a route handler takes (request, context); a fourth positional argument means untyped plumbing. No current page trips any of the three.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: Catch-all, deliberately last. Everything the sets above do not name: lib/notebook-pipeline.ts (77 lines of type declarations and const tables - PIPELINE_STAGES, GRAPH_NODES, GRAPH_EDGES - imported by both lab components; it declares no functions at all, which is why cs returns "score": null for it rather than a number), the three TypeScript/ESLint/PostCSS config modules (next.config.ts 8 lines, eslint.config.mjs 18, postcss.config.mjs 7 - all three also return "score": null), the JSON and Markdown cs cannot read (package.json, tsconfig.json, renovate.json, package-lock.json, README.md, diagrams/README.md), the five unreferenced Next.js template SVGs under public/ (file.svg, globe.svg, next.svg, vercel.svg, window.svg - no tracked file references any of them), and any directory a future change introduces. All 23 rules are pinned at 1.0 with framework thresholds for the detected language, so a new directory - a tests/ tree, a .github/ workflow, a second lib module with real logic - starts under the full guardrail and has to earn any relaxation with a measured rule set of its own.

rule_sets.rules_doc: Full weight for the remainder, and this is also where the missing test surface is handled rather than faked. There is no test file in this repository today (no test_*/*.test.*/*.spec.* anywhere, no test runner in package.json), so a test rule set written now would match zero files and be a policy about nothing. Instead any test file that appears lands here under all 23 rules at 1.0 - including the seven structural smells and also Low Cohesion, Primitive Obsession and String Heavy Function Arguments - which is stricter than the standard test profile, never looser. When the first test file lands, that is the moment to add a dedicated test glob at the documented 7-at-1.0 / 3-at-0.0 weights, ahead of this set, with its measured justification.
